# 2000A Question 1 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Explain**]{.task-verb} how cardiac output is measured using a thermodilution technique?
:::

Also asked in: [2005B Question 13](/content/exams/anzca/2005/B/13/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2010A Question 15](/content/exams/anzca/2010/A/15/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Explain**]{.task-verb} the indicator-dilution principle and the actual measurement sequence. Relate injectate properties and the temperature–time curve to cardiac output, then identify assumptions and sources of error.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Conservation Principle and Indicator Dilution

### Catheter, Injectate and Temperature Measurement

### Temperature–Time Curve and Cardiac Output Calculation

### Assumptions and Sources of Error

### Advantages and Limitations
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
Half of the candidates passed this question. Main points required included a definition of cardiac output, a definition and description of the Fick principle, an accurate description of the technique, a description of the temperature/time curve generated, advantages and disadvantages, and errors in the technique. Common omissions were failure to describe the Fick principle, the site of injection, to accurately draw the temperature/time curve, or appreciate that the area under the temperature/time curve is inversely proportional to the cardiac output. Many candidates also did not state advantages and disadvantages of the technique.
:::
